nodes.text: INSTANT · ON-DEVICE AI The provided document outlines the specific rules, powers, and requirements regarding the United States Constitution. Main Points: 1. Legislative Power: The U.S. Congress (Senate + House of Representatives) holds all legislative authority; no state may enter into treaties or grant letters without this consent. 2. Presidential Authority: The President must approve bills before they become law, but the Senate has sole power to try impeachments and propose/concur amendments. 3. Executive & State Powers: The Constitution vests executive power in the President; states may not lay duties or taxes on imports without congressional consent, which must serve national purposes. 4. Constitutional Crimes: Treason is defined as levying war or aiding enemies, with convictions requiring two witnesses or confession in open court. Congress grants punishment for treason but forbids Attainder of Treason from causing Corruption of Blood or Forfeiture unless during the attainted individual's life. 5. New States: New states can be admitted to the Union only if they secure the consent of legislatures and the Congress, without forming a new state through joining existing ones unconsented.
